concepts.why: Name against passages: Daniel 2:44 is about the God of heaven setting up a kingdom that shatters the others, not about kingdoms arising; it already stands under 'An everlasting kingdom'. Daniel 8:20–21 names the ram and goat as Media-Persia and Greece; set beside Daniel 2 and 7 under one heading it invites the mapping of the four kingdoms (Babylon, Media-Persia, Greece, Rome, or Greece as the fourth), which readers of every kind part on (academic, Reformed, Baptist/dispensational, Catholic). Daniel 2:38–40 and 7:17, 7:23 say the concept and name nobody beyond what the verses say.

Name against passages: the name is 1 Samuel 8:11, what the king will take. Deuteronomy 17:16–17 says what the king must not do (a law, not a warning of what he will do), and belongs with 17:18–20 under 'He who rules in the fear of God' (move it there; the passage is then Deuteronomy 17:16–20). Judges 9:14–15 shares only 'reign over us'; the thornbush's reply is a condition, not a manner of the king's ruling, and reading Jotham's fable as a warning about kings is an interpretation the verses do not state (academic, Reformed). After the change the concept is 1 Samuel 8:9, 8:11, 8:14–17, 8:18.

concepts.name: The King on Zion
note_fixes: Matthew 21:5: replace the note 'Say to the Daughter of Zion' (it does not say reigning) with 'See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey' (exact quotation of the verse)
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'Reigning on Mount Zion' is Isaiah 24:23 and Micah 4:7; Psalm 99:2 (Great is the LORD in Zion), Zechariah 9:9 and Matthew 21:5 (your King comes to the Daughter of Zion) do not say reigning, so the name says more than they do. The King on Zion (Psalm 2:6 'installed My King on Zion') is what all eight say in plain words. Matthew 21:5 stays beside Zechariah 9:9 as the passage that says the same words; the concept makes no claim that one fulfils the other.

concepts.name: The kingdom of God has come upon you; the kingdom of God is in your midst
concepts.why: Name against passages: only Matthew 12:28 and Luke 11:20 say 'has come upon you'. Luke 17:20–21 says 'is in your midst' (and the Greek behind 'in your midst' can also be read 'within you'; the original does not settle it), so the shorter name says what one passage says and the others do not. Naming both sayings in the verses' own words keeps all three passages without choosing a reading of Luke 17:21 (Baptist/dispensational and academic readers part on it). Luke 17:20 also stands in 'The kingdom is not ...'; that overlap is welcome.

secondary_or_links: Throne → enthroned between the cherubim: Psalm 99:1 says 'enthroned above the cherubim', not between; Psalm 80:1 and 2 Kings 19:15 say between. Rename 'Throne → enthroned above and between the cherubim' (or drop Psalm 99:1, which already stands in 'The LORD on His throne'). Reason: name says more than one of its passages.

Scepter → from Judah, from Israel: Psalm 110:2 says 'from Zion', so the name does not cover it. Rename 'Scepter → from Judah, from Israel, from Zion' or drop Psalm 110:2 (it stands in 'The King on Zion').
Other secondary concepts and the links list: no change. 'Image of God' is a fair link for the Rule → over the creatures of the earth entry; the entry makes no claim about what the image is.
